segments: 16 Chronography of Barhebraeus.
to this [Moses]:
and he fled to Arabia to Reuel the Midianite.
And when he was forty years old,
he took Zipporah, the daughter of Jethro, son of Reuel the Midianite, son of Medan, son of Jokshan, son of Abraham by Keturah his wife.
The commentators, however, say
that Jethro is Reuel.
And at this time occurred the third flood in Thessaly in the days of Deucalion;
and a great conflagration in Cush in the days of Phaethon;
and the renowned war of the Chaldeans with the Phoenicians;
and Eunomus discovered divination {OCR? / *music?*};
and Menander discovered comedy;
and Chiron and Asclepius [discovered] medicine.
And when Moses was eighty years old,
that is, in the four hundred and thirtieth year of the Promise,
he was commanded by God to bring out the Hebrews from Egypt.
And when the Hebrews crossed through the sea on dry land,
Pharaoh Psonos,
who succeeded Amenophis,
and all his army were drowned in the Sea of Suf (the Red Sea).
Now the Egyptians who did not go forth with Pharaoh,
when they saw the destruction of those who went forth,
each made for himself the work that was found in his hands into a god, and worshipped it,
as though on its account he had been restrained from going forth, which had been the cause of destruction.
And in that same year Moses fought with Amalek,
and went up into the mountain in the third month,
and received the Law and judgments for Israel.
And from the time God said to Abraham:
"Know of a surety that your seed will be a stranger and a sojourner in a land that is not theirs,"
four hundred and thirty years of servitude are reckoned,
as it is written in the Book of Exodus.
And Paul also testifies [to this],
even though in the first book, of Genesis, only four hundred years is written.
And from Adam until the death of Moses there were three thousand eight hundred (and four hundred) and fifty-one years,
according to Annianus the monk, with whom this compilation agrees.
According to the Septuagint, however,
three thousand eight hundred (and four hundred) and eighty-two [years];
and according to the Syriac and Hebrew,
two thousand four hundred and twenty [years].
For he was in Egypt forty years,
and in Midian forty years,
and in the desert forty years.
